result.note: Tests the Will for Peace 2026 exercise (host, venue, participants, India's stance) and the IBSAMAR format; skipped the analysts' framing as speculative.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the “Will for Peace 2026” naval exercise held in January 2026:
items: It was held off Cape Town, with South Africa as host.
Iran was among the participating countries.
India's Ministry of External Affairs described it as a regular, institutionalised BRICS activity.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. On 17 January 2026 the MEA called the exercise entirely a South African initiative, not a regular or institutionalised BRICS activity, and noted that not all BRICS members joined. Iran's participation drew US-side criticism, and Pretoria launched an inquiry into it.
questions.source: South Africa’s “Will for Peace 2026” naval exercise ran from January 10–16, 2026 off Cape Town, after warships began arriving around January 9.

questions.prompt: In January 2026, explaining its absence from a South African-hosted naval exercise, India's Ministry of External Affairs cited IBSAMAR as its standing maritime format. IBSAMAR brings together India with which two countries?
questions.explain: IBSAMAR is the India–Brazil–South Africa maritime format, last held in October 2024. The MEA pointed to it while stating that India had not taken part in previous South African-led drills of the Will for Peace kind.
questions.source: pointed to IBSAMAR (India–Brazil–South Africa) as its standing maritime format (last held October 2024).
